input.quote: 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
input.rationale: Section 22.1 permits unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems — walk-away territory and a failure of the fallback (no frequency limit, no notice). Sections 22.2 and 22.3 partially mitigate: 22.2 already keeps audit costs with Vendor unless underpayment exceeds five percent (preferred threshold) and bars direct access to Customer systems, which contradicts the access grant in 22.1. We therefore replace 22.1 with the preferred frequency, notice, business-hours, off-site and independent-auditor/confidentiality limits and delete the remote-access language, leaving 22.2 and 22.3 intact.

mappings.element: Vendor may audit no more than once in any 12-month period.
Vendor must give at least 30 days' written notice of an audit.
Audits are conducted by an independent auditor.
The auditor is bound by confidentiality obligations.
Audits are conducted off-site where possible.
Vendor bears audit costs unless underpayment exceeds 5 percent.
mappings.quote: Vendor bears audit costs unless the audit establishes an underpayment exceeding five percent for the audited period, in which case Customer will pay reasonable audit costs and the undisputed shortfall.

mappings.element: Vendor has no direct access to Customer systems for an audit.
mappings.quote: Vendor and its auditor may not access Customer systems directly, Customer Data unrelated to usage, privileged material, or another supplier's confidential information.

proposal.summary: Limit Vendor audits to once per 12 months on 30 days' written notice, in business hours, off-site where possible, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, and delete remote system access.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept unlimited, unannounced audits with remote access to our systems, so we have limited audits to once in any 12-month period on 30 days' written notice, in business hours, off-site where possible and through an independent auditor bound by confidentiality. Section 22.2 already keeps audit costs with Vendor unless underpayment exceeds five percent and bars direct access to our systems.

ops.oldText: Vendor may audit Customer at any time without notice and may remotely access Customer's systems and records for that purpose.
ops.newText: Vendor may audit Customer no more than once in any 12-month period, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, off-site where possible, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.
